subject: Marketplace legal / PO routing clarifications for private offer activation
messages:
From: Sasha Nguyen <procurement@acmecloud.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: marketplace-ops@acmecloud.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: PO mechanics for private offers (Redwood Inference)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for walking us through the listing requirements last week. Finance here is getting ready to issue a Purchase Order for Redwood's private offer, but we need a couple of confirmations before they can proceed:

- Legal entity name and remit-to address exactly as it should appear on the PO.
- Vendor tax ID (TIN) and a copy of your W-9 (or equivalent).
- Do you prefer to receive a single consolidated PO for the total committed value, or monthly POs for consumption invoices?
- Any special billing instructions or reference codes required by your accounting team (e.g., project code).

If you prefer, we can route the PO through the AWS Marketplace Private Offers workflow (our default) — in that case we will need your Marketplace Seller ID and confirmation that Redwood accepts Private Offer billing terms (Net 30 unless otherwise negotiated).

Attached is our standard private-offer purchase template for reference.

Appreciate a quick reply so procurement can start the paperwork.

Best,
Sasha Nguyen
Procurement Lead, Acme Cloud
Attachments: acme_private_offer_template.pdf (PDF, 84KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Nguyen <procurement@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PO mechanics for private offers (Redwood Inference)

Hi Sasha — thanks for the note. Quick answers and a few clarifying questions below.

1) Legal entity and remit-to (exact):
   Redwood Inference, Inc.
   1212 Redwood Lane
   Suite 400
   Palo Alto, CA 94301

2) Tax ID: 94-3176881 (we'll attach a signed W-9).

3) Preferred PO model: Our standard is a single consolidated PO for committed/contracted value when customers are purchasing reserved capacity or a contracted private offer. For consumption-based deals that are billed monthly via marketplace metering, we accept monthly POs but prefer a primary master PO referencing the deal id so finance can tie invoices back to the commitment.

4) Billing/reference code: Please add "Deal: DL-8392" in the PO notes and cc finance@redwood.ai on the PO.

5) Private Offer vs Direct Invoice: We can accept either, but a Marketplace Private Offer is preferred for AWS because it preserves the billing flow and simplifies tax handling. For Azure and GCP there are partner-center / marketplace program nuances — Ben, can you confirm partner-center paperwork for Azure?

6) Payment terms: Net 30 is acceptable; any deviation should be routed through Lauren Bishop (Finance).

Attaching our signed W-9 and an internal note describing Partner Center requirements for Azure (Ben has more detail).

Next steps: If you can confirm whether Acme will cut a single PO tied to the private offer or monthly POs, we'll route signatures internally and confirm Seller ID for the private offer flow.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_w9.pdf (PDF, 23KB), partner_center_notes.docx (DOCX, 12KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PO mechanics for private offers (Redwood Inference)

Kim / Vanessa — quick clarifications from ops/legal side: 

- Azure Marketplace: we'll need to complete the Microsoft Partner Center registration and have the legal team sign the Microsoft Commercial Marketplace Agreement (MCMA) before we can accept publisher-billed invoices. That typically adds ~7–10 business days.
- GCP Marketplace: supports both direct invoicing and marketplace billing; we should indicate preference in the PO.
- For AWS Private Offers: we need Acme to send the private offer via AWS with the Seller ID field populated. Once that's sent, AWS will link the offer to your account and we can accept.

I attached a short checklist I use for finance to process partner POs — includes the required fields (entity, remit-to, TIN, seller id, invoice email). Ben

Attachments: acme_po_processing_checklist.txt

From: Acme Cloud Marketplace Operations <marketplace-ops@acmecloud.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sasha Nguyen <procurement@acmecloud.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PO mechanics for private offers (Redwood Inference)

Hi Kimberly / team,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for attaching the W-9. We plan to issue a single master PO for the contracted private offer value and then route monthly metered invoices against that master PO — that should satisfy our internal controls and keep invoicing simple. We'll: 

- Raise master PO referencing Deal: DL-8392 to Redwood Inference, Inc., remit-to address as provided.
- Create the AWS Private Offer using your Seller ID (please reply with the Seller ID when ready).
- Set payment terms to Net 30; we'll copy Lauren as the finance approver.

One additional ask: our procurement team requires a signed Marketplace Partner Letter (we've attached a short template). Can Redwood sign and return? If you prefer, we can accept confirmation via DocuSign.

We'll send the PO PDF and a DocuSign packet for the partner letter once we receive the Seller ID and a confirmation of the preferred PO structure (master PO + monthly invoices).

Best,
Marketplace Ops Team
Acme Cloud
Attachments: acme_private_offer_template.pdf (PDF, 84KB)
